title: Invert Binary Tree
statement: Given the `root` of a binary tree, invert it — swap the left and right child of **every** node — and return the root. The result is the mirror image of the original tree.

example.why: Every node's children are swapped, so each level reads right-to-left.

idea: Mirroring a whole tree sounds big, but at one node it is tiny: just swap its left and right child.
Do that swap at **every** node and the entire tree is mirrored. Recursion visits every node for us.
Recipe for a node: swap its children → invert the left subtree → invert the right subtree. An empty node (None) needs nothing.

complexity.timeWhy: Every node is visited once and does a constant amount of work.
complexity.spaceWhy: The recursion stack is as deep as the tree's height h (log n if balanced, n if it is a chain).

steps.text: Our example: **`root = [4,2,7,1,3,6,9]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
At node **4**: swap its two children. Now node 7 is on the left and node 2 on the right — their whole subtrees move with them.
Now mirror everything underneath node 4's left child (node 7).
At node **7**: swap its two children. Now node 9 is on the left and node 6 on the right — their whole subtrees move with them.
Now mirror everything underneath node 7's left child (node 9).
Node **9** is a leaf: both children are empty, so swapping them changes nothing.
This child is empty (None). There is nothing to invert, so return straight away. This is the base case that stops the recursion.
Left side of node 7 is done. Now mirror its right child (node 6).
Node **6** is a leaf: both children are empty, so swapping them changes nothing.
Everything under node 7 is mirrored. Return to its parent.
Left side of node 4 is done. Now mirror its right child (node 2).
At node **2**: swap its two children. Now node 3 is on the left and node 1 on the right — their whole subtrees move with them.
Now mirror everything underneath node 2's left child (node 3).
Node **3** is a leaf: both children are empty, so swapping them changes nothing.
Left side of node 2 is done. Now mirror its right child (node 1).
Node **1** is a leaf: both children are empty, so swapping them changes nothing.
Everything under node 2 is mirrored. Return to its parent.
Done — the answer is **`[4,7,2,9,6,3,1]`**. Every node's children are swapped, so each level reads right-to-left.
